method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All fifteen translated content blocks defining and illustrating set-theoretic enumeration and enumerability.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A finite set displayed as a_1 through a_n corresponds bijectively to the first n natural numbers, and an infinite set is enumerated by a bijection with Nat.
samples.checks: Finiteness, distinctness, both correspondence directions, n-1 and the full-Nat condition remain present.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An enumeration of A is a bijection onto A whose domain is either an initial natural-number segment or all natural numbers.
samples.checks: Bijection, range, domain alternatives and the displayed initial segment are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A is enumerable exactly when it is empty or has an enumeration; it is nonenumerable exactly when it is not enumerable.
samples.checks: Both biconditionals, the empty-set case and the negation are explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Identity enumerates Nat, successor enumerates the positive naturals, and the doubling and odd-successor maps enumerate the even and odd naturals without enumerating Nat.
samples.checks: Domains, codomains, formulas, even/odd order and failure of surjectivity onto Nat are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The alternating ceiling formula enumerates the integers as 0,-1,1,-2,2,..., with the equivalent even/odd cases unchanged.
samples.checks: Ceiling direction, signs, table entries and both piecewise branches match the source.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Binary unions and, by induction, finite unions of enumerable sets are enumerable.
samples.checks: Both exercises retain their hypotheses, unions and induction variable n.

limitations: T060 and T062 are descriptive Marathi renderings without exact specialist attestation.
No independent linguistic certification has been performed.
